findings.title: Home page carries no machine-readable date
findings.evidence: Examined 2 pages; the home page has no visible date, no schema dateModified or datePublished, and no HTTP Last-Modified header, so its currency cannot be established from the response. The About page carries all three.

suggested_action.summary: Emit a dateModified on the home page so its currency is establishable without guessing.
suggested_action.what: A schema.org dateModified on the home page, matching an HTTP Last-Modified header.
suggested_action.where: The home page template at http://localhost:8000/index.html.
suggested_action.why: Nothing in the response says when the page last changed, so a system deciding between this page and an older third-party description of the brand has no recency signal to prefer it by.
suggested_action.how: Populate dateModified from the content's own last edit, not from the build timestamp. A date that changes on every deploy is not a freshness signal; it is noise, and it makes every future genuine change indistinguishable from a rebuild.
suggested_action.mechanism: Recency arbitration: a datable page can be preferred over a stale external description of the same facts.
suggested_action.success_criteria: The home page response contains a dateModified that changes when the page's content changes and not when it does not.

evidence_refs.observation: dates.visible_dates is empty; schema_date_modified, schema_date_published and http_last_modified are all null

false_positive_controls_applied: checked all three date sources before concluding the page is undated
excluded pages whose content is inherently undated, such as a contact page with no substantive claims
exceptions_checked: evergreen pages whose content genuinely does not change, where a stale-looking date would be worse than none
